label: I: Empty PQ-heavy (preloading)
description: After preloading 1M keys, this read workload is dominated by empty point queries over skewed key prefixes, with a smaller share of uniform lookups on existing keys.

label: II: Interleaved inserts, deletes, PQs, updates
description: An insert-heavy workload that interleaves uniform inserts, point deletes, empty point queries, and updates within a single execution phase.

label: III: Multi-distribution update and PQ (preloading)
description: After preloading 1M keys, updates follow a skewed Zipfian access pattern while point and empty-point queries stay uniform — a workload where different operations use different distributions.

label: IV: Update and range delete-heavy (preloading)
description: After preloading 1M keys, it pairs Zipfian-skewed updates with range deletes in equal measure, exercising point writes alongside range invalidations.

label: V: Insert-heavy with skewed prefixes
description: A single-phase, insert-dominated workload whose keys cluster around skewed prefixes, with a small fraction of point queries reading them back.

label: A: Update heavy
description: Balanced read and update workload with an initial insert phase.

label: B: Read heavy
description: Read-heavy workload with a small update slice.

label: C: Read only
description: Read-only YCSB workload after the initial insert phase.

label: D: Read latest
description: Read-latest YCSB workload with inserts and point queries.

label: E: Short ranges
description: Scan-heavy YCSB workload with inserts and range queries.

label: F: Read-Modify-Writes
description: Read-modify-write YCSB workload with point queries and merges.

label: 1: Multi-phased dynamic
description: Three sequential phases shifting from write-heavy to read-heavy: Zipfian inserts with point deletes, then uniform empty point queries, then a balanced 50/50 mix of inserts and range queries.

label: 2: Interleaved multi-distributional
description: A single interleaved phase mixing five operations — inserts, latest-distributed point queries, empty point queries, uniform point deletes, and Pareto-distributed range deletes — each from a distinct distribution to stress systems under mixed, concurrent load.

label: 3: Near-sorted ingestion
description: Pure ingestion of near-sorted keys: data arrives mostly in order (like a time-series store) with controlled disorder — 1% of keys displaced by up to 10% of the dataset — to test tolerance to near-sortedness.

label: 4: Slow phase transitioning
description: Three phases that gradually shift from write- to read-heavy — inserts fall 70%→50%→30% as point and range queries rise — with range-query selectivity varying uniformly between 0.1 and 0.2.

label: 5: Discrete phase transitioning
description: A sharp two-phase switch from write-heavy (90% inserts) to read-heavy (70% point queries), evaluating how a system responds to a sudden change in access pattern.

label: 6: Variable entry size
description: A balanced 50/50 insert and point-query workload where key and value sizes each vary uniformly from 32B to 256B, simulating document or blob stores where entry-size variability drives I/O and memory usage.

label: 7: Skewed access
description: Skewed access where a small set of hot keys dominates — half the workload inserts keys clustered on a hot 10% prefix, and half issues heavily skewed point queries — typical of caching and real-time analytics.

label: Test 1: Bulk Load (Random Order)
description: Loads 900M keys into an empty database in random order to measure raw ingestion performance.

label: Test 2: Random Read
description: Measures performance of random point lookups on the 900M key dataset.

label: Test 3: Multi-Random Read
description: Models RocksDB's multi-get read pattern as random point lookups over the 900M key dataset; tectonic issues the reads individually, with no batched multi-get primitive.

label: Test 4: Range Scan (Forward)
description: Randomly selects starting points and iterates forward over keys to measure scan performance.

label: Test 4b: Reverse Range Scan
description: Randomly selects starting points and iterates backwards through the key space.

label: Test 5: Overwrite
description: Measures random overwrite performance on an existing database, triggering LSM-tree compactions.
